documentation.title: Oblique frictional impact between two free deformable bodies
documentation.description:
A deformable disk strikes a deformable block OBLIQUELY, with Coulomb friction, under large sliding. Nothing is fixed anywhere: both bodies are free, the only force in the model is the contact traction, and the disk arrives with a large tangential velocity so it SLIDES along the block while the contact patch forms, grows and travels.
THE INVARIANT: -contactForceX / contactForceY = mu.
The primary surface is the block's FLAT top, so the contact normal is exactly (0,1) in every configuration and the reported resultant splits without ambiguity into contactForceY (normal) and contactForceX (tangential). Coulomb's law fixes their ratio at -mu wherever every point slips -- negative because the resultant is the traction on the SECONDARY body and friction opposes its motion. It is an exact statement about the friction law, not a fitted number, and it holds whatever the impact does to the pressure distribution or the patch size, which is what makes it assertable at all: no closed form exists for the pressure in a transient elastic impact. Under slidingType="small" it is exact to twelve digits; under "large" it differs in the fourth digit because the normal is then taken on the DEFORMED surface and the block's top is dented by the impact, so it tilts slightly.
WHY IT SLIDES THROUGHOUT, so the inequality is an equality: friction can change the disk's tangential velocity by at most mu times the normal impulse over the mass, which is small against its tangential velocity. Nothing ever sticks and numStickPoints stays 0. tangent="consistent" for that reason -- every point slips, the regime where the default degrades as the slide grows, and the complementary hazard (failure when points stick) does not apply.
The patch FORMS, GROWS and TRAVELS: 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 6 -> 7 -> 8 active points, with numPoints, numCells and numContactElements all moving with it. Under slidingType="small" all three are FROZEN by definition, so these integers gate large sliding rather than merely exercising it.
